notes:
I couldn't do this research. The first batch of page requests went over this session's tool limit, and after that every further fetch or search was blocked. So I didn't read Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes), StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or any of the other allowed sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for each point. That means I have no notes on Isaiah 19 to give you. Writing them from my own knowledge would break the rule against filling gaps, so I haven't.

If you start a new session, I'll fetch the pages one or two at a time so I stay within the limit. I'd go in this order:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Isaiah 19), Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Barnes pages for Isaiah 19, and Precept Austin's Isaiah 19 page.
2. **Where traditions differ:** mainly vv. 18–25 (the "City of the Sun," the altar in Egypt, and "Egypt My people"), looking for how each side reads the promise to Egypt and Assyria, whether as already fulfilled, about the church, or still to come. Sources would be Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Gill as the Baptist voice, and Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY and LCMS for the Reformed, Baptist and Lutheran views.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on v. 18 ("City of the Sun" against "City of Destruction") and on vv. 19–25, a Bible Odyssey article on Egypt in the prophets, and New Advent / Church Fathers material on Isaiah 19:1. Older Christian writers often linked that verse to the Holy Family's flight into Egypt.
